page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It provides 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the n2-highcpu-2 operates in the lower tiers of performance. In stress-ng testing, single-core performance scored 1399.29 and multi-core performance scored 1841.88. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 102.26 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 11.78 GB/sec. Geekbench results align with these findings, showing a single-core score of 1111.0 and a multi-core score of 1311.0. The instance exhibits lower-tier performance in specific workloads, such as software compilation with clang and ray tracing.

With 2.0 GB of RAM and no local storage, this instance is constrained for memory-intensive applications or large-scale database operations, as reflected by a Passmark database score of 687.89. However, it supports advanced CPU instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES cryptography. The dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable execution for lightweight, compute-focused tasks. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for entry-level computational workloads, basic text processing, or small-scale web serving where high memory capacity is not required, but dedicated CPU resources are preferred over shared-core alternatives.
